note: Datetime Now is a zero-configuration widget enhancement: no settings, no configure route, no permissions, no Drush, no plugins, no config or state. It implements hook_element_info_alter() to append a #process callback (Drupal\datetime_now\ElementInfoAlter\DatetimeElementInfoAlter) to the core 'datetime' render element, injecting a 'Now' button (class datetime-now inside datetime-now-wrapper) plus the datetime_now/datetime_now JS library. Because the trigger is the datetime ELEMENT, the button appears on the datetime_default widget and the daterange_default widget (start+end) but NOT on datetime_datelist (which renders the 'datelist' element). There is no per-field config to read, so medium cases inspect the live element_info / field setup, and hard cases have the agent add a datetime/daterange field whose widget renders the datetime element (the observable prerequisite for the Now button). Verify scripts assert the field+widget and that datetime_now's callback is wired into the datetime element.

evals.prompt: I installed the Drupal contrib module datetime_now. Where is its configuration page and how do I turn on the 'Now' button for my Date/time fields?
evals.expected_output: Datetime Now has no configuration page and no configure route. Simply enabling the module adds a 'Now' button to every core Date/time widget that renders the 'datetime' element (datetime_default and the daterange_default widget) — there is nothing to configure per field.

evals.prompt: How does the datetime_now module add its 'Now' button to Drupal Date/time widgets — which hook and which render element does it alter?
evals.expected_output: It implements hook_element_info_alter() and appends a #process callback (DatetimeElementInfoAlter::process) to the core 'datetime' render element. That callback adds a 'Now' button (class datetime-now) and attaches the datetime_now/datetime_now JS library.

evals.prompt: Does the datetime_now 'Now' button appear on the Date/time 'Select list' (datetime_datelist) widget? On which Date/time widgets does it actually show up?
evals.expected_output: No. datetime_now alters the core 'datetime' render element, so the button appears on the datetime_default ('Date and time') widget and the Datetime Range daterange_default widget (start and end). The datetime_datelist ('Select list') widget renders the 'datelist' element, which datetime_now does not alter, so it gets no button.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the Article content type has a Date/time field that will render a datetime_now 'Now' button on its edit widget. Inspect the live default form display for Article and give the machine name of that field.
evals.expected_output: field_dtn_known: in core.entity_form_display.node.article.default it uses the datetime_default widget, which renders the 'datetime' element that datetime_now augments with a Now button.

evals.prompt: The Article field field_dtn_elem on this site renders a 'Now' button on its Date/time edit widget. By inspecting the running site, determine which enabled module adds that button to the datetime form element.
evals.expected_output: The datetime_now module. Inspecting the 'datetime' element info (plugin.manager.element_info) shows a #process callback whose class is Drupal\datetime_now\ElementInfoAlter\DatetimeElementInfoAlter, added via hook_element_info_alter().

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, add a Date/time field named field_dtn_task to the Article content type and configure its default edit form so that, thanks to the datetime_now module, editors get a 'Now' button on it. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create a datetime field storage/field field_dtn_task on node/article and set its component in core.entity_form_display.node.article.default to the datetime_default widget (which renders the 'datetime' element datetime_now augments with the Now button).

evals.prompt: On my Drupal site I want Article authors to enter a start and end date/time for an event, and I want a quick button that fills each one with the current time (the datetime_now module provides it). Add a date range field called field_dtn_period to Articles and set it up so those quick-fill buttons appear. Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create a Datetime Range (daterange) field field_dtn_period on node/article and set its component in core.entity_form_display.node.article.default to the daterange_default widget. Because that widget renders 'datetime' sub-elements for start and end, datetime_now adds a Now button to both.
